The windows are misty, but covered in drawings. Players receive cards with different designs and keep only one for their window. They then give the other cards to their neighbor. After 12 turns, each player has a magnificent window filled with drawings that will come to life in front of them: the balloons float up, the vehicles drive out and the leaves fall down. Only some of the drawings can earn you points. The most beautiful and valuable drawing is the flower, but watch out for the monster who keeps on trying to eat it. Misty is a tactical draft game, in which to win, one must anticipate where the cards will move and watch the other players’ windows. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Gameplay 2.1 Construction Phase 2.1.1 Placing Rule 2.2 Card Activation Phase 2.3 End of the round and scoring Overview This is a 2-4 players draft placing game. Each player lays out a 12-card window and score from it. A game contains several rounds. The first player to win 2 rounds is declared the winner. A round contains two phase: Construction and Card Activation . Gameplay Construction Phase Each player start with 6 cards in hand. Chooses one card from your hand and puts it in front of you simultaneously. Pass the remaining cards to the left and do this again. Once you run out of hand, Draw another 6 cards and do the same thing but pass to the right instead. Once you run out of cards again, each player has a full 12-card window in front of them. Placing Rule All card must be placed in the right direction. Card must place adjacent to at least one other card in orthogonal direction or diagonal direction. Each window must finally form a grid with 3x4 or 4x3. Card Activation Phase Once the construction phase is finished, each player activates their window in turn. Each time you choose one card with arrow to activate: move the card one space in the direction indicated. If it moves outside the window space, it is immediately eliminated. Once every arrow card has been moved, the monster eats the flower: the flower is remove and the monster is moved to its spot. End of the round and scoring When everyone is done activating their window, count your scores as follow: - An empty space gets 0 point. - A space with two or more overlapping cards makes a blur and doesn't score any points. - The flower scores 2 points. - Each smile cards scores 1 point. Two smile cards side by side horizontally score extra points (3 points in total). - Each other card scores 1 point, including the monster. [Rating: 2/10] Really uncompelling game of hoping you find the exact thing you want. I didn't find the artwork that great either.

[Rating: 3/10] Very uninteresting drafting exercise. Optimizing your tableau offers a small glimmer of positivity, but generally the lack of variation of cards bogs the game down.

[Rating: 3/10] Giochino di carte abbastanza banale e senza troppa originalità. Gli elementi che lo caratterizzano sono la casualità nella pesca delle carte e il draft iniziale. La grafica delle carte riporta gli immaginari disegni di un bambino su un vetro tutto appannato, dovremo cercare di posizionare i disegni in maniera ottimale per poi spostarli (se richiesto) e quindi fare più punti possibile. Gioco poco longevo con ambientazione completamente inesistente, non mi ha per nulla conquistato.

[Rating: 3/10] Misty is an awful game, I did not enjoy it at all and everyone who played it agreed it was terrible.  Some people seem to find enjoyment from this but I don't know why?!

[Rating: 3.5/10] The points are almost pre-defined by the inicial draw of the cards. Unbalanced cards give the game obvious decisions. At least the game is really fast, so it's pretty much painless. The good thing: moviments after the drafting.

[Rating: 4/10] Good for kids, not really my thing. I just bought this not to pay the shipping ;) so no complaints there, and I guess I am going to play it with my daughter more, who knows?

[Rating: 4/10] Some of the same ideas as the charmingly hard Mesozooic, simplified until there's almost nothing there. A cute art conceit (shapes doodled on the window in condensation after rain) but nothing else.

[Rating: 4/10] I just did not find the use of the draft in a tableau interesting enough. I get it is targeted at smaller kids, but my youngest daughter played it and was done with it.
